styles.name: Bullet Time
styles.description: A frozen moment: in a bright white high-speed-photography studio a striped orange ball bounces in and drops into a big white bowl of cobalt-blue liquid, and mid-splash TIME STOPS — the crown, its beaded rim, the spray of droplets and the ripples hang perfectly still while the camera keeps sweeping a near-full circle around them. Two clocks: timewarp.js maps video time t to WORLD time w(t) (run, freeze, reverse, forward, release, with linear rate ramps, so w is piecewise quadratic and exact), and separately lays out the camera arc. Every world thing — the ball's bounce and plunge, the lathe-profile crown with pinching lobes, ballistic droplets, floor splats, the cavity, ripples and the rebound jet — is a closed-form function of w, never stepped, so time can be scrubbed backward (the splash un-happens) and forward again. Sound follows w: every bounce, impact, pinch and droplet landing is cued wherever w(t) crosses it (reversed re-crossings included), with jog ticks while scrubbing and a pitch-dropping whir into the freeze. A two-track overlay gauge (CAMERA vs WORLD) shows the decoupling.
styles.summary: **Look.** A bright white high-speed-photography studio: pale calibration-grid floor fading into white haze, four softboxes on stands.

styles.name: City Lights

styles.name: Cymatics
styles.description: Sound builds the picture: a dark anodised square metal plate on a speaker driver, dusted with tens of thousands of bright warm-white sand grains, on a clean light lab bench under a strong soft key light. A tone plays and the sand dances (grains on antinodes hop, grains on nodal lines sit still) and gathers into the crisp geometric nodal-line figure of that frequency (Chladni figure, w = cos(n pi x)cos(m pi y) +/- cos(m pi x)cos(n pi y)); the pitch steps up and the figure shatters and re-forms into a more intricate one. Every grain's settled position per mode is precomputed (seeded Newton steps onto the nodal set + a little spread); motion is a closed-form blend with per-grain delay plus a hop proportional to the local plate amplitude. The plate flexes slightly with the mode shape. Sustained tones, a sand hiss and lock chimes come from the same mode list.

styles.description: Night-sky fireworks over a harbour whose bursts form planned shapes. styles.description: A hand-drawn pencil flipbook riffled under a thumb: a thick pad of cream paper clamped under a walnut bar on a warm, bright desk, most of its pages bent back over the bar in a fan pinched by a stylised thumb. The thumb lets the pages go one at a time; each page curls (real bent-page geometry: hinge angle + bend + corner twist, integrated along the page every frame), falls toward the viewer and slaps flat with a small bounce, so the pencil drawing on the pages comes to life. Every page carries its own procedural graphite drawing from one planner: bold soft-edged lines with graphite grain, light construction circles and arcs, hatching, smudges and a pencil page number, with line boil (each page's strokes wobble by a page-seeded displacement). A real pencil can finish a line on the first page. The release plan gives every flip a paper tick and slap in sync, from a slow page-by-page flip to a full-speed riffle at 12 drawings a second.

styles.name: Fogged Glass
styles.description: A steamed-up window pane: behind it a bright sunrise town (sky, balloons, skyline, river, lamps) painted once into a sharp texture and once into a pre-blurred, milky, bokeh-dotted 'fogged' texture. An unseen finger writes in the condensation: the fog mask is a pure function of t — for every pixel, clear = max over planned strokes of (drawn by now x re-fogging decay), redrawn from the plan each frame into a small mask canvas (no accumulation). The pane shader shows the fogged texture where the mask is 0 and the sharp scene where it is 1, with a beaded boundary, a refracting lit/shaded water rim along every wiped edge, a wet sheen on fresh strokes and lens-like drops that gather under the strokes and run down with stick-slip, leaving clear trails. Old strokes narrow and fog over; a palm sweep clears the whole pane and the last fog evaporates. Squeaks, drip plinks, the palm swipe and the reveal chime come from the same plan (fogplan.js).
styles.summary: **Look.** A steamed-up window pane in a wooden frame.

styles.name: Galton Board
styles.description: A Galton board (bean machine) on a bright oak desk: a glass-fronted maple frame, an enamel-blue backboard with a triangular field of brass pegs, a walnut hopper with a brass spout and polished steel balls. A seeded, precomputed ball plan (plinko.js) gives every ball its left/right choice at each peg row, a closed-form path (drop, one parabolic hop per row, ballistic fall into its bin, two small bounces) and a stack slot, so the histogram grows ball by ball into a bell curve. Pegs flash and swell when struck; every peg tick, release click and bin landing (one marimba note per bin) is a sound cue from the same plan. A red enamel bell curve is drawn on the glass over the finished stacks.
styles.summary: **Look.** A Galton board (bean machine) standing on a bright oak desk against a pale wall: a glass-fronted maple frame (6.3 m wide, toy-scale so a 0.14 m ball reads at 1080p), an enamel-blue backboard, a triangle of 78 brass pegs between...

styles.name: Hanging Mobile
styles.description: A kinetic hanging mobile in a bright skylit gallery: thin black wire arms with end loops, fine threads and flat painted sheet-metal plates (disc, leaf, crescent, triangle, custom outlines) in bold red, yellow, blue, black and white turn slowly in still air, while crisp soft shadows drift across the white wall behind. Balance is computed for real: every arm's pivot is solved from the weights on each side (weight = plate area), so hanging a new shape or changing a weight tilts that arm and every arm above it, the whole structure swings and re-settles with a closed-form damped oscillation, and a re-balance slides each pivot loop to the new centre. Small engraved tags hang under the plates; a museum-label overlay carries the words.
styles.summary: A kinetic hanging mobile in a bright, skylit white gallery.

"add one thing and everything shifts", hierarchies and org structures (the tree *is* the hierarchy), calm openers and section breaks,

exact quantities and charts (the tilt is a picture of imbalance, not a gauge), long text, step-by-step processes,

styles.name: Impasto
styles.description: Thick oil paint in the post-impressionist manner: on a primed woven canvas, short fat brushstrokes with real 3D relief (bristle grooves along the stroke, raised edge ridges, a blob where the brush lifted, two colours dragged together) are laid one after another along a seeded swirling flow field — halo rings around a glowing moon and stars, a big double swirl in the sky, contour strokes on rolling hills, flame strokes up a cypress, dabs for a village — in ultramarine, cobalt, chrome yellow, viridian and orange. A raking light sweeps across so the paint ridges cast tiny shadows and catch glossy highlights; the camera can drop low and close so the canvas reads as a landscape of paint. Then the swirls flow: every stroke slides along its own precomputed streamline as a pure function of t. One InstancedMesh (~1,100 strokes), each instance bent into a constant-curvature arc in the vertex shader, with per-pixel bristle normals in the fragment shader; a planner schedules the stroke order and the brush sounds from the same list.
styles.summary: **Look.** Thick oil paint in the post-impressionist manner, seen as sculpture.

styles.name: Impossible Geometry
styles.description: Sunlit pastel-stone architecture under an orthographic camera that lies: a real open staircase whose two ends line up from one magic angle into an endless loop, with a little walker climbing for ever, then the camera swings off-axis and the loop splits open to show the trick. Flat three-tone faces, fine edge lines, a soft ground shadow, a calm sky.

styles.name: Infinity Mirror
styles.description: Recursion you can count: a framed light box on a dark gallery wall holds one real layer (a hoop of large warm and coloured bulbs plus a small glowing figure) between a rear mirror and a half-silvered front glass. Each reflection is REAL instanced geometry (generation n = the real layer reflected n times: alternately flipped, stepped back by the cavity depth, dimmed by mirror x glass reflectance per bounce, so deep copies go dim and green), so the tunnel can grow one generation at a time, anything placed in the real layer ripples into every copy, and the camera can push through the front glass and fly down the tunnel past copy after copy. A small tilt between the mirrors turns every step into a rotation about the mirrors' hinge line: the straight tunnel bends, and at pi/ringCells it closes into a ring, so the flight curves all the way round and arrives back in front of the box. One soft pluck per new generation, each quieter, lower and duller, comes from the same plan.
styles.summary: **Look.** A framed light box on a dark gallery wall in a pool of warm light.

styles.name: Inflatable
styles.description: Glossy inflated vinyl and mirror-foil balloon objects in a bright seamless studio: puffy pillow letters, numbers, arrows, stars, hearts and speech bubbles with a flat welded seam round the edge, pinched scalloped corners, tight wrinkles radiating from the seam, a little valve and strong soft-box highlights. Inflation is a pure function of time: each object starts as a flat, crumpled outline on the floor, its skin is rebuilt every frame from fill(t) — thickness swells from the middle outward, wrinkles tighten and fade, it stands up, overshoots and wobbles to rest with a squeaky stretch. Objects also deflate (sag, fold, sink), bump neighbours and squash on contact, get squeezed so the air shifts to one side, or float up on ribbons and bob. Words inflate letter by letter; air hiss, rubber squeaks and a boing come from the same plan.
styles.summary: **Look.** Glossy inflated objects in a bright warm-white seamless studio: puffy pillow letters, numbers, stars, hearts, arrows and speech bubbles made of candy-coloured vinyl (clearcoat skin) or mirror foil (gold / silver / rose).

styles.name: Ink Wash
styles.description: Brush-and-ink painting coming to life on a large sheet of soft fibrous off-white paper with deckled edges, lying on a felt mat beside an ink stone, a water bowl and a brush rest. A real 3D brush tilts and presses along each planned stroke: ink appears exactly as far as the brush has travelled, width follows pressure, the stroke starts wet-dark and runs dry into streaky flying white, then the edges feather outward and the tone lightens as it dries. Broad grey washes bloom and settle with darker edges, a drop of indigo or vermilion spreads into a wet wash as a soft flower, and an abstract seal is pressed at the end.
styles.summary: **Look.** A brush-and-ink painting coming to life on a large sheet of soft, fibrous off-white paper with deckled edges, lying on a charcoal felt mat.

styles.name: Inkblot
styles.description: Symmetric inkblots on heavy cream card in bright, soft daylight (original blots, not the Rorschach plates). Glossy beads of wet ink (black plus crimson and indigo) drip onto one half of an open sheet; the other half folds shut on a real hinge, a wooden press rubs it down, and the sheet peels open on a perfectly mirrored blot with noise-feathered bleeding edges, a pale capillary halo and darker pooled rims. The ink is a closed-form field (a sum of smooth elliptical blobs and voids from a seeded plan, warped by paper-fibre noise) evaluated per pixel in the card's shader in half-space, so both halves show the same function; wet ink is glossy and domed and dries to matte. Then the same blot is read several ways: pencil outlines (graphite on paper, chalk-white over ink) draw themselves on, suggest one thing, fade, and suggest another. The blot never changes, only the reading. Drip plips, the fold, the press, the peel and every pencil stroke are scored from the same plan.
styles.summary: **Look.** A heavy cream card (3.6 x 1.7 m, toy-scale) on a pale blue-grey desk in bright, soft daylight.

styles.name: Kintsugi
styles.description: Break and mend: a glossy celadon tea bowl on pale oatmeal linen in soft window daylight falls, cracks along a seeded fracture (weighted spherical Voronoi of warped surface directions, so each crack runs through the whole wall) and splays into a dozen-odd shards that tip outward, clink down on the cloth convex side down and rest; they rise along arcs and slot back home; then molten gold runs ALONG the seams from one pour point on the rim (a Dijkstra arrival field over the seam network, baked into a texture), glowing hot at its leading tip and cooling to a raised, glossy, slightly irregular gold bead, with a few chipped-out spots filled flush with gold. Seams are evaluated per fragment, so they stay crisp at any distance. Ends on a slow orbit with the gold catching the light. Shard landings, returns and every seam junction the gold reaches are sound cues from the same plan.

styles.name: Layer Print
styles.description: A generic desktop 3D printer in a bright workshop: an open aluminium frame, a dark gridded heated bed, a gantry that rises with the part and a print head with a glowing brass nozzle laying down coloured filament. The object grows layer by layer and every layer is drawn as its real toolpath — outer perimeter, inner perimeter, then infill (scan lines on the floor, a zigzag inside the wall) — from a slicer plan (slicer.js): the part is sliced once into timed polylines, the whole bead geometry is built once with a per-vertex deposit time, and a frame shows every bead whose time has passed, cut exactly at the nozzle. The planned path of the current layer shows ahead of the nozzle as a thin line, fresh plastic glows for a moment, and the finished part keeps fine layer ridges. Print time is compressed honestly: timing stages speed up layer after layer. Stepper servo/whir cues per move and a tick per layer change come from the same plan.
styles.summary: **Look.** A generic desktop 3D printer in a bright workshop (toy scale: the machine is ~5 m wide so kit lights and text sizes apply; read 1 m as ~5 cm).

styles.name: Lichtenberg
styles.description: Fractal wood burning: a pale maple board on a dark slate workbench mat with two copper electrodes clamped to it. A high-voltage discharge burns a branching Lichtenberg figure into the wood between them. The whole tree is planned once, seeded (space colonisation from the first electrode, half-width from downstream length, a burn time per node, dead ends everywhere and exactly one path that reaches the second electrode) and baked into a distance + burn-time field; at time t each groove is drawn up to its burn front: white-blue arc at the tip, glowing orange ember just behind, near-black char with a soft brown scorch halo after. When the one path connects, a return stroke flashes back along it, the channel widens and stays glowing. Smoke wisps, flickering tip glints, the crackle, the hum and the connection crack all come from the same plan.
styles.summary: **Look.** Fractal wood burning.

styles.name: Mixing Console
styles.description: A vintage analogue recording console shot close and low across its surface in warm studio light: brushed-aluminium channel strips between walnut end-cheeks, long-throw faders, coloured rotary knobs with pointer lines, lit square push-buttons, LED bargraphs, a meter bridge of needle VU meters with warm backlit cream faces, white console tape with hand-written channel names, a jog wheel, and tape reels turning behind in shallow focus. Rows are iso-contours of an exact distance transform of the picture's regions, traced by marching squares and resampled at tile pitch. Each tile is a slightly irregular, slightly tilted 3D chip (stone matte, smalti glossy, gold-leaf glass metallic), so when a low light sweeps across, the gold tiles glint one after another in a travelling shimmer. styles.description: The classic chain-reaction demonstration on a bright blue sports-hall floor: a neat grid of toy-scale spring traps (pale wooden board, yellow pedal, red paddle hammer), each loaded with two white ping-pong balls. A seeded planner precomputes every landing, ballistic arc and snap; the same plan drives the picture, the snaps and ball ticks in the score, and a row of dots that doubles generation by generation.

styles.name: Multiplane Cel
styles.description: Classic hand-painted cel animation shot on a multiplane camera: a storybook landscape painted in flat gouache with visible brush strokes (sky, far hills, a meadow with a path and a cottage, a tree grove, dark foreground foliage) and one inked-and-painted cel bird animated on twos, each layer on its own sheet of glass. Inside the picture the camera pushes down through the stack and the layers part with strong parallax; pulled back, the truth: a vertical steel rig of six glass panes with lamps between the shelves, peg bars on every tray and a film camera looking straight down from the top. Sliding one pane sideways changes the picture (a grove slides off and reveals the cottage). Flat unlit paint, crisp black ink and flat colour on the cel with a soft cel shadow, faint glass sheen and a few dust specks.

styles.name: Murmuration
styles.description: A dusk sky (warm horizon, cool zenith, low sun glow, a thin dark tree line with pylons for scale) where thousands of tiny near-black birds wheel as one living cloud. Nothing is placed: each bird has a closed-form position at time t — a blend between its point in the previous and next formation (seeded volumetric samples of a blob, a ribbon, an arrow, a ring, glyphs or an icon), plus a smooth 3D noise flow so the flock swirls and breathes, plus travelling density waves that bunch the birds and bank them toward the camera so a dark band rolls through the cloud. Edges stay soft with stragglers; the whole flock sways and turns as a body. Birds are two-triangle silhouettes that flap with a per-bird phase and point along their velocity (finite difference of the same closed form). The sound is a wing-rush whose level follows flock speed, a low whoosh per density wave, sparse distant calls and a gentle pad.
styles.summary: **Look.** A dusk sky — warm apricot at the horizon, rose band, dusky lavender, cool blue-violet zenith — with a low sun glow on the right and a thin dark horizon (near tree line, hazy far tree line, a row of lattice pylons with sagging w...

styles.name: Music Box
styles.description: The open movement of a music box, shot macro in warm bright light on pale wood: a lathe-turned brass cylinder studded with steel pins turns slowly toward a polished steel comb; each pin presses one tooth down and lets it go, the tooth springs back, rings visibly and warms in colour for a moment; a hand crank with a wooden knob drives the cylinder through a brass pinion and a worm spins a two-vane governor. One note list (tune.js) places every pin (angle around the cylinder = when, position along the axis = which tooth), moves every tooth in closed form and writes the score, one pitched bar note per pin at the exact release time. Engraved track rings and bar lines on the cylinder make it read as a score. Captions on an ivory plate with a brass edge.
styles.summary: **Look.** The open movement of a music box, shot macro in warm bright light on pale wood (toy-scale: the cylinder is 2.6 m long so one pin reads at 1080p).

styles.name: Nesting Dolls
styles.description: A family of lathe-turned, hand-painted, lacquered wooden nesting dolls on a pale birch table in soft window daylight. One lathe profile scaled per level makes every shell (hollow lid + cup with a bare-wood tenon, or solid for the smallest). The big doll's head twists, lifts off with a wooden pop and is set down behind; a smaller doll rises out of the cup and hops aside; the head goes back on; again and again, faster and higher-pitched as they shrink, down to the solid one. Each doll wears the same geometric pattern with less detail than its parent, and a belly emblem of concentric rings — one ring per doll still inside — around a yellow dot. A camera dive into the smallest doll's dot comes out of the biggest doll's dot onto the whole family lined up large to small. One plan (nest.js) drives visibility, every pose, the line-up and the score.
styles.summary: **Look.** A family of lathe-turned, hand-painted, lacquered wooden nesting dolls on a pale birch table in soft window daylight (toy scale: the biggest doll is 2.2 m tall so the smallest, 0.6 m, still reads at 1080p).

styles.name: Newspaper Press
styles.description: A broadsheet front page as a physical object: warm newsprint with show-through and fold creases, heavy black serif headlines, column rules, greeked justified body text and procedural halftone photos — spun in, printed live by an ink roller, circled in red grease pencil.

styles.name: Op Art
styles.description: 1960s optical art on a white gallery wall: one large hard-edged panel of pure black-and-white pattern that the eye reads as depth and motion. Vertical stripes whose spacing and black/white duty are warped so a sphere seems to bulge out of the flat wall, and the bulge travels; a clear acetate sheet of rings slides over a ringed panel so moiré bands sweep much faster than the sheet moves; a Vasarely-style grid of checker squares and circles whose size and colour step ring by ring into a dome, then flip into a tunnel, with red and cobalt accents; and a reveal where the camera walks off-axis to show the 'dome' is flat paint on a flat board. Every pattern is analytic in one shader (fwidth antialiasing, stripes >= ~16 px wide, fade to mean grey below Nyquist), camera locked except the reveal, no strobing.
styles.summary: **Look.** 1960s optical art, after the *methods* of Bridget Riley and Victor Vasarely (the compositions are our own, not copies of any work).

styles.name: Origami
styles.description: Japanese paper folding on a calm oak desk: single sheets of two-sided kami paper fold on screen, crease by crease, into crisp faceted models lit by soft window light, labelled with ink-printed washi strips.
styles.summary: Japanese paper folding on a calm light-oak writing desk in soft window light from the front-left.

styles.name: Paper Marbling
styles.description: Paper marbling in a shallow white enamel tray on a bright pale-wood studio table, seen from above with a slight tilt. A glass pipette lets drops of ink fall onto thickened water; each drop spreads into a flat disc and pushes every earlier colour outward into concentric rings; a stylus is drawn back and forth and a comb is pulled across, and the rings stretch into feathers and chevrons; a sheet of paper is rolled onto the bath, peeled away carrying the pattern (the bath is left almost clean), lifted and turned to the camera as a finished print. The pattern is not simulated: it is a composition of closed-form area-preserving marbling deformations (ink-drop displacement, tine-line and comb displacement, from the mathematical marbling literature) applied in plan order; a fragment shader inverse-maps each pixel through the operations so far, the current one partially applied by its progress, so any frame is a pure function of t. Flat saturated inks (indigo, vermilion, ochre, teal, cream) with a slightly denser rim per drop; soft daylight; water plips, soft drags and paper sounds come from the same plan.
styles.summary: **Look.** Paper marbling (ebru / suminagashi method) in a shallow navy-rimmed enamel tray of thickened water on a pale wood studio table, seen from above with a slight tilt, in soft daylight.
styles.avoidFor: anything needing numbers, text inside the picture, precise diagrams, or dark/moody looks.

styles.name: Pendulum Wave
styles.description: A classic pendulum-wave demonstration on a bright, cool-white bench: a row of 15 large glossy balls, saturated rainbow by index, hangs on V-strings from a curved wooden beam carried by two A-frames, each pendulum a little shorter than the last. Pendulum k completes (N + k) swings in one cycle, so released together from a wooden plank they drift into a travelling snake wave, split into groups, look like chaos, and then all return to one line at the same instant, where the plank catches them. Everything is a closed form of t (wave.js): angles, string lengths (from the periods), motion-trail ghosts (the same formula at earlier times), a lamp on the bench under each ball that flashes at its centre crossing, and one pitched bar note per crossing, so the sound goes from a chord strike to a ripple and back to a unison. A planned clock can freeze the motion: a camera flash, and the frozen positions fly down into an overlay 'fingerprint' card.
styles.summary: **Look.** A classic pendulum-wave demonstration on a bright, cool-white bench (toy scale: balls 0.43 m across, the row 7 m long, so one ball reads at 1080p).

demos.topic: "How AI tags word order".

styles.name: Pin Art
styles.description: A giant pin-impression toy (pinscreen): a clear acrylic frame holding a dense grid of thousands of slim polished metal pins with domed heads, on a dark matte desk under a strong low raking key light and a soft coloured rim light, so any relief pushed into the pins reads as a field of bright pin heads and long shadows. Polished steel by default, brass and anodised colour finishes. Shapes are pressed through the field as a pure function of time: every pin's extension is sampled from a target height field built from text and icons (distance fields with a rounded bevel), a hand, a ball rolling underneath, ripples from a tap, bars rising as columns of pins, terrain or a bitmap; transitions morph between fields with a wave that travels across the grid (per-pin delay from position, eased, tiny overshoot, metallic settle) and pins drop back in a cascade. The camera orbits low so relief and shadows read.
styles.summary: **Look.** A giant pin-impression toy (pinscreen) on a dark matte desk.

styles.name: Pinball Table
styles.description: An electro-mechanical pinball playfield seen from the player's end, glass off: glossy printed wooden playfield with original abstract art, chrome rails and a steel ball, rubber-ringed posts, mushroom pop bumpers with coloured caps, a drop-target bank, rollover lanes, slingshots, two flippers, a plastic ramp and lit inserts under the playfield, plus a backglass with mechanical score reels. The ball follows a planned contact schedule; every contact lights lamps, drops targets and steps the reels.
styles.summary: An electro-mechanical pinball machine seen from the player's end with the glass off.

styles.name: Point Cloud Scan (LiDAR)
styles.description: A LiDAR scan made only of measured dots on near-black: a scanner head on a tripod turns while a thin bright laser fan sweeps the room and the world appears dot by dot, coloured by range (cyan near, yellow, magenta far) and shaded by return intensity. No surfaces are ever drawn: objects (a figure, a chair, a bicycle, a plant, a table, walls with a door and a window) exist only as ray targets. The scan shows the tells of a real terrestrial scan: rings and lines that spread with distance, and scan shadows — empty holes behind every object that the laser could not see, hidden from the scanner's own viewpoint and dramatic once the camera orbits away. A second scan from another tripod fills the holes.
styles.summary: No surfaces at all: the world exists only as measured dots laid down by a terrestrial laser scanner on a tripod.
styles.goodFor:
how machines perceive (LiDAR, depth cameras, self-driving, robotics, 3D scanning, photogrammetry), "the map is
not the territory", blind spots / missing data / sampling, surveying and digital twins, measurement vs. reality.

warm or human-story topics, anything that needs readable surfaces or textures, text-heavy beats, bright
daytime moods, many small objects (under ~0.2 m they turn to a few dots).

demos.topic: a LiDAR scan made only of dots.

styles.name: Pottery Wheel
styles.description: A potter's wheel in a sunlit plaster studio: wet, glossy grey-brown clay spins on a steel wheel head inside a pale splash pan, a window's light patch on the wall behind it and a shelf of finished glazed pots out of focus. The clay is one lathe surface whose profile is a pure function of t, morphing between named key profiles (lump, cone, opened cylinder, bowl, collar, vase) bottom-up like a real pull, with its volume held constant so it is always the same clay. Spin reads through slip streaks, throwing rings that appear once it is thrown, a lumpy off-centre wobble that damps as it is centred, and marks on the wheel head. A wooden rib on a handle rides the wall exactly where the profile is changing fastest. At the end the wheel slows and a brush sweeps glaze on in a spiral from foot to lip. Wheel hum pitched by spin speed, wet squelches at shape changes and the brush come from the same plan.
styles.summary: **Look.** A potter's wheel in a sunlit plaster studio.
styles.goodFor:
"same thing, reshaped" stories — fine-tuning, refactoring, iteration, one resource many uses, training as
shaping, craft and patience, before/after transformations of a single object, product evolution.

anything that needs text on the object.

styles.name: Ship in a Bottle
styles.description: A bright modeller's bench in daylight: a large clear glass bottle lies on a wooden cradle, and a small wooden sailing ship (walnut hull with a red boot and a cream strake, three masts, pleated paper fan sails, thread rigging) is built outside the bottle with its masts hinged flat against the deck. The long thin bundle slides through the narrow neck on a wire, settles onto a blue putty sea, and one thread running out of the neck is pulled: the masts swing upright fore to aft, the sails fan open and the rigging draws taut. A cork goes in. One plan (rigging.js) turns thread length pulled into every hinge angle in closed form, places every thread point (taut or sagging by its slack), carries the insertion path, proves in Node that the folded bundle clears the neck and the raised ship clears the glass, and writes the score.

styles.name: Star Chart
styles.description: A planetarium night: a deep blue-black dome of sky with a visible gradient, a Milky-Way band and thousands of seeded stars (size and colour variety, gentle deterministic twinkle) over a low dark horizon of hills, trees and an observatory; antique celestial-atlas graphics drawn over it in fine gold line — coordinate grid, ticked ecliptic, constellation stick figures, engraved figure outlines, small serif star names. The invented sky turns about a pole so stars rise, drift and trail; chosen stars brighten one by one, gold lines draw between them into original constellations (each a concept, each star a part), an engraved figure fades up, a name plate writes on, a presenter's arrow sweeps to what is being named, and a dashed line connects two constellations.

styles.name: Sticky Notes
styles.description: A workshop wall in a daylit studio: a bright whiteboard in an aluminium frame covered in square paper notes in soft colours, each with a short marker word, curled at the free edge over a soft shadow, plus dot stickers, marker-drawn lanes, headers and boxes, and a pad of notes on the ledge. Notes behave like real sticky notes as pure functions of time: they peel off the pad (the curl travels in from the free edge), fly, slap flat strip-first and flap down to a resting curl, then peel and hop between columns, cluster by colour, collect dot votes and ripple in a travelling breeze.

styles.name: String Art
styles.description: Curve stitching on a nail board: a dark walnut-stained board (well lit, warm workshop light) with rows and a ring of brass nails; saturated cotton thread is wound nail to nail by a moving needle tip, each thread drawn up to the current point with a tiny wrap round every nail it turns on. Every thread is perfectly straight, yet together they make smooth curves — parabola fans between two nail rows, a cardioid from a ring (chords m -> 2m, wound as continuous doubling cycles). Threads stack in winding order, cast thin shadows on the board and catch a soft sheen; nails catch highlights. A winding planner (winding.js) is the single source of truth for picture and sound: a soft pluck per thread, pitch rising with its index.
styles.summary: **Look.** An upright, mid-walnut board (5.4 x 3.0 m, toy scale; horizontal planks from the kit wood texture with visible grain, slim moulded frame) brightly lit by warm workshop light from the upper left plus a cool front fill.

styles.name: Tessellation Morph
styles.description: A wall of interlocking cut-paper tiles in two alternating colours, bevelled and layered so it is clearly 3D, where every tile is the same creature and the creature morphs smoothly (plain tile -> fish -> bird) without ever leaving a gap. Each lattice cell is a parallelogram whose opposite sides are one shared curve: what bulges out of one side is cut from the other, so any curve tiles. Key shapes are pairs of curves; the morph interpolates them point by point, and because each edge carries its own morph value the wall can show the whole transition in one frame, left to right. Eyes, gills, a beak and wing lines fade in only near a key shape. Tiles can leave the wall: a row of birds lifts off, folds along its body line to flap, and flies out, leaving bird-shaped holes. Whooshes, clicks and flutters come from the same morph plan.
styles.summary: **Look.** A wall of interlocking cut-paper / painted tiles in two strongly contrasting colours (cream, raised 24 cm; navy, 13 cm), every tile the same creature.

styles.name: Thermal Camera
styles.description: A handheld thermal imager's view of ordinary objects: the picture is temperature, not light. Plain geometry (a desk, a PC tower with its side open, a monitor, a keyboard, a mug, a hand) rendered with an unlit temperature shader through an ironbow palette (black, deep purple, magenta, orange, yellow, white). Things glow because work is happening in them: heat sources switch on and approach their temperature exponentially, a conduction front creeps along heat sinks and boards with sqrt(t), exhaust air rises as a warm plume, a hand pressed on the desk leaves a print that spreads and fades, and everything slides back down the palette when the work stops. Slightly cooler at grazing angles (emissivity) so forms still read. Sensor character: soft low-resolution blur, a faint pixel grid, gentle seeded noise. Imager HUD on the overlay: centre crosshair with a spot reading, a vertical colour scale with min/max, and a SAMPLE DATA tag because every temperature is invented.
styles.summary: A handheld thermal imager's view of ordinary objects.
styles.goodFor:
"work shows up as heat" — load, effort, activity, energy use; what is busy vs idle in a system; ideas that
  "warm up" as they activate; things spreading from a source (conduction front); traces left behind (residual heat, memory,
  footprints); before/after "it cooled down".
- **Avoid for:** exact colour branding (the palette IS the data), anything needing many readable labels in-world, real
  measurements (temperatures here are invented — keep the SAMPLE DATA tag unless the user supplies real data), materials or
  textures (everything is one shader by design).
styles.avoidFor:
exact colour branding (the palette IS the data), anything needing many readable labels in-world, real
  measurements (temperatures here are invented — keep the SAMPLE DATA tag unless the user supplies real data), materials or
  textures (everything is one shader by design).

styles.name: Tiny Diorama
styles.description: A whole little world on one floating bevelled tile: layered grass/soil/rock slab sides, chunky rounded buildings, lollipop trees, toy cars and peg people in matte pastel plastic, one soft sun, contact shadows, tilt-shift and a narrow near-isometric camera.
styles.summary: A whole little world on one floating 16:10 tile, like a designer's desk model or a mobile-game map piece.
styles.goodFor:
"where does X go / how does X flow" systems (networks, supply chains, energy, water, logistics, cloud),
cities and neighbourhoods, onboarding maps, numbered step walkthroughs over places, and friendly product or infra explainers.
styles.avoidFor:
precise data or charts, dark or serious subjects, organic or photoreal scenes, anything bigger than one tile
(this style is about a contained world), and dense text.

demos.topic: "Where does your prompt go?" on one floating diorama tile.

styles.name: Tiny Planet
styles.description: A whole world on one small rotating globe that fills the frame: a faceted low-poly sphere on a warm cream backdrop, lit by a fixed sun so the right limb is always a blue night crescent. A bare grey gridded ball turns under a fixed camera; streams of small word chips rain onto it, and from every landing point a front spreads along the surface: land rises out of the ball, colours in (sea, sand, grass, rock, snow), then trees, houses, roads and clouds pop up, and warm lamps come on as they turn into the night side. One planner (globe.js) places everything in latitude/longitude, computes when each front reaches each vertex and feature in closed form, and writes the score.
styles.summary: **Look.** One small faceted low-poly globe (6 m across, toy scale) on a warm cream backdrop with a soft pale halo behind it.

demos.topic: "A model builds its world from what it reads".

styles.name: Toy Brick
styles.description: Generic interlocking plastic construction bricks shot as toy-photography macro: glossy moulded ABS bricks, plates, slopes, arches, rounds and tiles on a stud grid with hairline seams and tiny bevels, crisp soft-box reflections, tinted transparent pieces, a studded baseplate on a pale studio table, shallow depth of field; everything is BUILT — bricks drop in bottom-up and snap down with a squash and a click.
styles.summary: A build made of **generic** interlocking plastic bricks (plain studs, no brand marks, our own peg-figure), shot like toy-photography macro on a pale studio table.
styles.goodFor:
anything explained as *assembly* — stacks, layers, pipelines, architectures (LLMs, networks, software stacks),
"building blocks of X", modular systems, step-by-step builds and teardowns, playful kids/edtech explainers.
styles.avoidFor:
organic or soft subjects, precise charts, serious/sombre topics, long copy, photoreal products.
Not voxel: voxel = same-size matte cubes as pixel art; this = varied glossy moulded parts that snap together.

demos.topic: "What's inside a large language model?" as a toy-brick tower you build.

styles.name: Typewriter
styles.description: A generic mid-century manual typewriter (no brand marks) on a pale wooden desk in daylight, shot close: sea-green enamel body, round cream keys in chrome rings, a U-shaped basket of steel type bars, a two-colour inked ribbon between two spools, cream paper on a black rubber platen. Words appear on the paper one struck letter at a time: the key dips, its type bar swings up and hits the print point, the ribbon lifts, the inked glyph is there when the bar falls back, and the carriage steps one column left. At the end of a line the bell rings, the lever throws the carriage back and the paper feeds up a line. Every strike, space, bell, ratchet tick and carriage stop is a sound cue from the same typing plan that drives the picture.

styles.name: Ukiyo-e
styles.description: Japanese woodblock printing in passes: a sheet of cream washi with kozo fibres lies on a pale hinoki bench against two wooden kento registration guides. Carved cherry-wood blocks swing down onto it one at a time like a lid, press (the key block gets a baren rubbing pass over its back), and swing up again to reveal the ONE flat layer each has left in register: first the black key line, then the sky bokashi gradation, Prussian blue, a second blue, ochre and pink, until an original great-wave-and-mountain seascape is complete; a red seal stamps it and the printed layers lift a few centimetres off the paper for a gentle parallax. Each block's underside carries its own inked relief (mirror-correct when it opens) and kento marks. Layers are multiplied onto the lit paper like transparent ink, so fibre and wood grain show in every flat colour and the key line survives every pass.
styles.summary: **Look.** Japanese woodblock printing, shown one pass at a time.

demos.topic: one woodblock print made in passes.

styles.name: UV Reveal
styles.description: Two-layer surface revealed by a moving ultraviolet torch: an ordinary printed page (illustration + dummy text) lies on a warm oak desk under bright room light and shows no trace of anything else. A hand-held UV torch switches on, the room light dims, and inside the torch's violet pool a hidden fluorescent layer glows — a repeating watermark lattice, neon contours, a code strip and a big stamp — in saturated cyan, green and magenta on deep violet paper. The pool position, its radius (torch height and beam zoom) and a short phosphor afterglow behind the moving pool are pure functions of t along a planned torch path (torchplan.js); in the shader the visible print sinks to deep violet and the hidden layer is added to the page's emission only where the pool or afterglow masks are non-zero. Final move: the room goes dark, the torch lifts away, the pool radius grows past the sheet and the whole hidden layer glows at once. Switch click, lamp hum, sweep whooshes, per-mark pings and the flood chime come from the same plan.
styles.summary: **Look.** An ordinary printed page on a warm oak desk under bright room light: a headline, a flat illustration, grey lines of dummy text.
styles.goodFor:
anything hidden in plain sight — watermarks, provenance, metadata, fingerprints, steganography, hidden
bias, fine print, "what the model also learned", forensic checks, security features. **Avoid for:** stories with no
"before" surface (the mechanic is the contrast between the two layers), dense data, anything that needs a bright frame
throughout (the UV beats are deliberately violet), long text in the hidden layer (marks must be big and few).
styles.avoidFor:
stories with no
"before" surface (the mechanic is the contrast between the two layers), dense data, anything that needs a bright frame
throughout (the UV beats are deliberately violet), long text in the hidden layer (marks must be big and few).

styles.name: Voxel Studio
styles.description: Voxel-art models on a pale studio sweep: thousands of bevelled same-size cubes on a strict grid, flat limited palette, thin dark gaps, neighbour-occupancy AO in the crevices, 5x7 voxel lettering, warm key + cool fill, narrow-FOV three-quarter camera; everything moves in whole-cube steps or assembles cube by cube.
styles.summary: A voxel-art model photographed in a studio.
styles.goodFor:
step-by-step processes and transformations (denoising, compression, pixels to images, building and assembling,
sorting), anything about grids, pixels, games, data cells or blocks, playful tech explainers, and counters and progress.
styles.avoidFor:
organic or soft subjects (faces, water, cloth), photoreal or premium product looks, long body copy (5×7 text
needs about 6 cubes per character), and smooth curves or precise charts.

styles.name: Why AI Matters — House
styles.description: The Why AI Matters channel package: a deep-navy newsroom studio with a faint floor grid, horizon line, haze and a reflective floor; extruded League Gothic capitals with paper faces and green/blue rim-lit bevels that rise letter by letter out of THE RULE (one thick electric-green bar that always draws on first and becomes plinth, underline, divider and progress bar); warm paper cards with serif headlines and Space Mono metadata; red reserved for the one thing that matters most; quick whip-pans between sets and rock-steady holds.
styles.summary: The **house style** for the Why AI Matters channel (host Ekello Harrid): the 3D form of its existing defaults.
styles.goodFor: idents, bumpers, lower thirds, chapter cards, key numbers, pull quotes, end cards and recurring segments.
styles.avoidFor: whole explainers with many objects (use another atlas style and add the overlay pieces), light or pastel topics, and real data shown without a source.

styles.name: Weather Map
styles.description: A broadcast weather map made physical: a raised relief model of an invented landmass (seeded coastline, hills, depth-shaded sea) on a studio table, soft cloud puffs floating above it casting shadows, and bold broadcast graphics on a glass layer above: white isobars from a pressure field, red warm and blue cold fronts with marching symbols, big H and L centres, flowing wind arrows, temperature bands draped on the land and weather icons that pop up over invented places. Fronts and pressure centres advance as functions of time; clouds and their shadows travel with them, and a place's icon and colour band change the moment its front arrives, while the camera sweeps like a broadcast fly-over.
styles.summary: A broadcast weather map made physical.
styles.goodFor:
trends moving through a system, forecasts, "what's coming", fronts of change (market mood, adoption waves, a
policy rolling out region by region), before/after across places, pressure building and releasing.
styles.avoidFor:
real geography or real weather (everything is invented by design; don't present it as a forecast), exact
quantities (temperatures are SAMPLE DATA, isobars carry no numbers), step-by-step processes (use subway-map / low-poly), more than
~6 named places (cards collide at 1080p).

demos.topic: "What's coming" on a physical broadcast weather map.

styles.name: Wind Walker
styles.description: A kinetic walking sculpture on a bright low-tide beach: a skeletal creature of pale plastic tubing, black cable ties and cloth sails whose twelve legs are identical planar bar linkages (a straight-line four-bar feeding a pantograph, solved in closed form by circle–circle intersections) hung on one shared crankshaft, each station a sixth of a turn later, so rigid sticks step in a travelling wave. Body travel and height are locked to the lowest foot, so planted feet do not slide; footprints and step thuds come from the same plan. Opens on ONE leg as a diagram in sea mist (ink centre-lines, crank circle, the foot's flat-bottomed loop traced as a glowing path), then the mist lifts to reveal the whole creature striding across the sand.
styles.summary: **Look.** A bright, pale beach at low tide under a blue-white sky.
styles.goodFor:
simple rigid rules producing lifelike behaviour; emergence from mechanism; "it looks alive but it's geometry";
many dumb parts making one smart motion (neurons → behaviour); embodied AI / robotics; anything "one input, many outputs in phase".
styles.avoidFor: dark or moody topics, dense text, data charts, anything needing more than one short caption at a time.

styles.name: Wireframe Hologram
styles.description: A sci-fi briefing-room hologram: additive cyan wireframes, point clouds and fresnel-rimmed scan-filled faces materialise bottom-to-top above a projector ring on a dark glossy table, with drifting scanlines, seeded glitch slices, HUD rings and amber highlights.
styles.summary: A sci-fi briefing-room hologram.
styles.goodFor: systems and data flow (networks, pipelines, graphs, architectures), "how X works" briefings, AI/tech/sci-fi topics, anything that builds up part by part.
styles.avoidFor: warm, organic or human topics; photoreal products; dense paragraphs; bright daytime moods; many colours (one accent only).

styles.name: Zen Sand
styles.description: A raked dry garden seen close: a shallow wooden tray of pale fine sand under a low raking morning sun, smooth dark stones and a sprig of moss. Everything is drawn IN the sand — a rake, stylus or rolling ball travels a planned path and the groove (soft ridges either side catching the light) appears exactly as far as the tool has gone; rake lines flow around stones as concentric rings, words and arrows are traced as grooves, and a flat board drags across to erase a region back to calm.
styles.summary: A raked dry garden seen close: a shallow wooden tray of pale fine sand on a dark table, one low raking morning sun from the back-left, smooth dark stones, a sprig of moss, pale wooden tools.
styles.goodFor:
calm explainers, focus/clarity/mindfulness-adjacent themes (secular), "clearing the noise", single words,
simple diagrams (arrows, circles, rings), paths and journeys, before/after with an erase beat.
styles.avoidFor:
dense text (one word or ~10 caps per beat), numbers-heavy content, fast cuts, lowercase, anything
needing colour coding (the palette is sand and stone), and religious imagery (keep it a garden, not a shrine).

demos.topic: "clearing the noise" in a raked dry garden.

styles.name: 3D Zoetrope
styles.description: Animation about animation: a bright toy turntable on a clean cream studio sweep carrying rings of small glossy sculptures, each ring holding N successive poses of one looping action (a red ball bouncing with squash and stretch on clear rods, a sprout in a terracotta pot growing, blooming and closing). Standing still it is a row of statues; spun up under continuous light it smears into a blur (deterministic multi-sample motion blur over a one-frame shutter); when a strobe locked to the spin snaps on, the room goes dark, a strobe lamp lights the disc and each station appears to animate in place; a slightly detuned strobe makes the whole animation creep slowly round the disc. Disc angle is a closed-form function of t (smoothstep speed steps, exact integral), so every frame is a pure function of time.
styles.summary: **Look.** Animation about animation.
